items.title: Epic Seven E7WC 2026 Knockout Stage Kicks Off on October 24
items.summary: ⓒ SmilegateSmilegate announced that the Knockout Stage of the Epic Seven World Championship 2026 (E7WC 2026) for Epic Seven will begin on October 24.
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ⓒ Smilegate Smilegate announced that the Knockout Stage of the Epic Seven World Championship 2026 (E7WC 2026) for Epic Seven will begin on October 24. A total of 16 players will compete in this stage, which serves as Round 2 of the main tournament.

The Knockout Stage will take place every weekend at noon for approximately four weeks, from October 24 to November 14. Like the Group Stage, it will feature a double-elimination format to determine the four finalists. The Grand Finals will be held on November 28 at the Lotte Cinema World Tower Super Plex in Jamsil.

The participating roster consists of 14 players who advanced through the Group Stage over the past two weeks and 2 players who earned direct seeds into the Knockout Stage. The seeded players, Hazamarei and MagicQi, earned their spots by placing first and second, respectively, in the newly established online league, Epic Seven Masters 2026.

Epic Seven is a mobile turn-based tactical RPG developed by Super Creative. In E7WC 2026, competitors will battle for the title of global champion through "World Arena," the game's real-time PvP mode.

The preceding Group Stage was held over four days on October 10, 11, 17, and 18. Defending champion XiaoXuenai fell to FN in the winners' bracket but managed to advance to the Knockout Stage by winning the final match. In Group E, Omega pulled off a comeback victory from a tough position by utilizing Salome, a hero capable of cloning enemy heroes.

All matches will be broadcast live in four languages on the official Epic Seven YouTube channel, Chzzk, and global Twitch. Smilegate will host Drops events for viewers on Chzzk and global Twitch while also giving away coupon codes during live streams. In addition, an in-game match prediction event will allow players to earn rewards by forecasting match outcomes.

items.title: ‘Epic Seven’ Heads for Steam Late Oct., E7WC Kicks Off
items.summary: This week, developer Super Creative and publisher Smilegate unveiled a host of details on their free-to-play role-playing game title 'Epic Seven'. Namely,
items.content:
This week, developer Super Creative and publisher Smilegate unveiled a host of details on their free-to-play role-playing game title ‘Epic Seven’. Namely, that the game will be launching on the Steam platform on 29 October (a demo is available as of this writing as well as part of the Steam Next Fest event!). Alongside this platform launch comes opening of the new “Foundry” server, which will help players quickly adapt to the game through various events that will come about.

Starting on the 29th, a Settlement Support Buff Event will provide various effects to accelerate Hero and account growth, including a 30% increase in EXP gained. Furthermore, players who reach Account Rank 70 will receive the Hero “Luna,” along with 20 free daily summons. There will also be bountiful login rewards and an event where players can earn Equipment, growth materials, and Hero skins based on points accumulated from playing Arena (PvP) content.

The new Foundry server can be accessed not only through Steam but also via the STOVE PC Client and mobile devices. Additionally, players can use their existing account data to play directly on Steam.

Heads up: play data from the demo will not carry over to the official release.

Moving onto the championship event which kicked off today: E7WC 2026 saw its first stream, with one scheduled for tomorrow and the next weekend after. Plus, another fan favourite character from ‘Chaos Zero Nightmare’ makes her way over to the game:

Celebrating its 6th year, the E7WC is a premier tournament that crowns the global champion of Epic Seven’s real-time PvP mode, World Arena. Top players from the Global, Europe, Korea, Japan, and Asia servers will compete, with all matches from the Group Stage to the Finals live streamed in four languages. This year’s Finals will be held on November 28 at the Lotte Cinema World Tower Super Plex in Jamsil, South Korea. The total prize pool is $100,000. The champion will take home $50,000, and a special in-game skin will be created for a Hero of their choice.

Taking place over four days—October 10 (Sat), 11 (Sun), 17 (Sat), and 18 (Sun)—the Group Stage will feature fierce clashes between 28 players who advanced through the grueling Preliminaries. Competitors will be divided into groups of four in a Double Elimination format, with the top two from each group advancing to the Knockout Stage. There, they will compete for the World Champion title alongside Hazamarei and MagicQi, who advanced directly to the Knockout Stage as the champion and runner-up of Epic Seven Masters 2026.

For fans watching the tournament via Twitch, Smilegate will host a Drops event and reveal exclusive coupon codes during the live broadcasts. Additionally, an in-game Match Prediction Event will allow players to predict the results and earn rewards.

Meanwhile, Epic Seven is introducing “Mei Lin,” a new collaboration Hero from the popular IP “Chaos Zero Nightmare” (CZN), in today’s update. Following “Haru” and “Renoa,” Mei Lin is the third collaboration Hero to join the roster, allowing players to experience her original charm perfectly captured within Epic Seven.

Epic Seven is available as a free-to-play title across PC via STOVE , iOS , and Android via Google Play —with the Steam client launching 29 October.

Enjoying DayOne ? Do us a favour, and make us a ‘ Preferred Source on Google ‘ – that way, you’ll only be delivered more gaming coverage from our team.

There’s plenty of ways to become a part of DayOne. Head over and let us know your thoughts in the Day O ne Forums , the perfect place to chat about games if you’re a little more old-school and prefer things in a longform form, and if you mainly play on PC, join our Steam Community to connect with other members and maybe make some new friends!

Prefer the chaos of live and fast moving conversation? Come and make some noise in the lively DayOne Community Discord Server instead. If you’re rocking a DayOne Membership, both places give special access for our supporters, and you’ll unlock a ton of exclusive content, just for you.

items.title: Epic Seven Announces Events for Its Official Steam Launch on October 29
items.summary: Ahead of its official Steam launch on October 29, the mobile RPG Epic Seven has revealed a lineup of events, including a new server called "Foundry" and a Steam demo available from October 8 to October 27.
items.content:
Details of the events planned for the official Steam launch of Epic Seven, a mobile RPG operated by Smilegate and developed by SUPER CREATIVE, were released on October 8 (Thursday). The official Steam service is scheduled to begin on October 29 (Thursday).

On October 29 (Thursday), Epic Seven will begin its official service on Steam, one of the world's largest gaming platforms, and the new server "Foundry" will open at the same time.

A series of events will also be held so that players can get used to the game quickly on the new server.

A settling-in support buff event starting on October 29 (Thursday) offers various effects that support the growth of heroes and accounts, including a 30% increase in EXP gain.

Players who reach account level 70 will receive the hero "Luna," and 20 free summons will also be available every day.

In addition, there will be an event in which players can obtain equipment, growth materials, and hero skins by earning and accumulating points through Arena (PvP) content, along with login bonuses.

The new "Foundry" server can be accessed not only through Steam but also through the PC client "STOVE" and on mobile.

Players can also use their existing account information as is to play on Steam.

From October 8 (Thursday) to October 27 (Tuesday), a demo of Epic Seven can be played on Steam.

The demo is available as part of "2026 Steam Next Fest" and lets players try the main story as well as battle content such as "Brawl," "Battlefield of the War God," and "Automaton Tower."

Progress made in the demo will not carry over to the official service.

The Epic Seven app can be downloaded from Google Play and the App Store. More information about the game is available through the official community and the official YouTube channel.

items.title: Epic Seven Pity: $302 to Guarantee a Hero [2026]
items.summary: Epic Seven's 1.5% base rate has no 50/50 — 121 pulls guarantees your hero for 02-18. See the full cost table and EV math.
items.content:
Epic Seven’s gacha has one feature that sets it apart from almost every other anime-style gacha on the market: there is no 50/50 coin flip. The short answer for anyone deciding whether to chase a specific hero is this – Smilegate sets the base rate for a 5-star hero at 1.5% per pull on a Covenant pickup banner, and backs that up with a hard, deterministic guarantee at 121 pulls that hands you the exact featured hero, not a random 5-star from the wider pool. Priced out in real money, that guarantee runs roughly $302 to $318 depending on how you buy your Skystones, based on Epic Seven’s own currency shop and current App Store pricing.

How Epic Seven’s Summon System Works The Base 5-Star Rate: What 1.5% Really Means Epic Seven’s Biggest Difference: No 50/50 Coin Flip The 121-Pull Hard Pity, Explained Pull-by-Pull Probability Table What It Costs: Skystones, Bookmarks, and the Math Between Them The Pity-Cost Table: Currency and Real Cash at Every Milestone Step-by-Step Expected Value Calculation Five Worked Examples: What Different Budgets Actually Buy How Epic Seven Compares to Other Gacha Pity Systems Myths vs. Facts About Epic Seven’s Gacha Is Chasing a Specific Hero in Epic Seven Worth It? Frequently Asked Questions What is Epic Seven’s base rate for a 5-star hero? Does Epic Seven have a 50/50 system? How many pulls does it take to guarantee a featured hero? How much does it cost to guarantee a hero in Epic Seven? Is it cheaper to buy Skystones in bulk? When does soft pity start in Epic Seven? Is Epic Seven’s rate disclosure considered reliable? Should I save Skystones for a specific banner, or spend as I go? Related Coverage That’s the headline. The rest of this piece walks through where those numbers come from, what a pull-by-pull probability curve looks like under the published 1.5% base rate, a step-by-step expected-value calculation, a worked pity-cost table priced in both Skystones and dollars, and five spending scenarios so you can judge whether saving up for one hero is worth it before you open your wallet.

Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

Epic Seven runs its gacha through “Covenant Summons,” which pull from a shared pool of heroes and artifacts. A single summon costs 5 Covenant Bookmarks, and Bookmarks are bought with Skystones, the game’s premium currency, according to BlueStacks’ Epic Seven beginner’s guide . The in-game shop sells 5 Bookmarks for 100 Skystones at the standard rate, or 50 Bookmarks for 950 Skystones as a bulk option, which works out to 95 Skystones per summon instead of 100, per Epic7DB’s currency guide .

The week's biggest stories in tech, gaming and security, in one email.

The banner that matters most for anyone chasing a specific hero is the Covenant “Drop Rate Up” banner, sometimes called a pickup banner, which rotates roughly every one to two weeks and features a single highlighted 5-star hero. As of early September 2026, that rotation included heroes like Uncharted Pioneer Politis on a Drop Rate Up banner starting September 3, and Lisette on a Mystic pull banner from late August, according to the Epic Seven Wiki’s heroes hub , confirming the game is still actively live-serviced with fresh banners rather than winding down.

Every Covenant pickup summon draws from a rarity table where the top tier, 5-star heroes, sits at a flat base rate of roughly 1.5% before any pity boost kicks in, according to a September 2026 update to the Epic Seven Wiki’s summons and pity guide . That rate has crept upward over the game’s history. Older third-party breakdowns from 2019 and 2020 cited figures closer to 1.25% to 1.4% for a 5-star hero, so the current 1.5% figure reflects a modest rate increase Smilegate has made to the base odds over time, not a number that’s stayed frozen since launch.

What makes that 1.5% figure different from base rates in most other gacha games is what happens after it hits. In games like Genshin Impact or Honkai: Star Rail, a 5-star pull is often followed by a second roll of the dice over which specific unit you actually receive. Epic Seven skips that step entirely on pickup banners, which is the single biggest reason its pity math is simpler to calculate than almost anything else in the genre.

Most modern gacha systems layer a 50/50 mechanic on top of their pity count: hit the top rarity, and there’s roughly a coin-flip chance it’s the character the banner is actually selling rather than a generic unit from the standard pool. Epic Seven doesn’t do that on its Covenant pickup banners. The Epic Seven Wiki states it plainly: “Covenant pickup pity is 121 pulls and there is no 50/50,” and that if the banner has a featured hero up, “the 121st yellow is that hero.”

That single design choice changes the entire cost calculation compared to a game like Genshin Impact’s 50/50 pity system , where losing the coin flip can force a second full pity cycle before you’re guaranteed the unit you actually wanted. In Epic Seven, once you’ve committed to a pickup banner, every pull that doesn’t land a 5-star still counts toward the same 121-pull counter, and there’s no branch where you land the top rarity and still walk away without the hero you were saving for.

Epic Seven layers a soft pity ramp on top of the flat base rate starting around pull 100, and that ramp climbs until it reaches a deterministic guarantee at pull 121, per the Epic Seven Wiki’s summons documentation. Put simply: if you haven’t landed the featured hero by your 120th pull on a given pickup banner, your 121st summon is that hero, full stop, no roll involved.

Smilegate hasn’t published the exact per-pull rate curve for the 21 pulls between where soft pity starts and where hard pity locks in, so this article doesn’t estimate specific percentages for that stretch. What’s confirmed is the start point (around pull 100), the endpoint (pull 121, guaranteed), and that the climb in between only raises your odds, never lowers them. That’s enough to build a conservative, fully sourced cost model without guessing at numbers nobody has published.

Using the flat 1.5% base rate that applies through pull 99 (before soft pity begins), the cumulative chance of landing the featured hero at least once follows the standard formula for repeated independent draws: 1 minus (0.985 raised to the power of the pull count). Here’s how that curve looks at common milestones.

items.title: Producer Kwang-jin Tak: "For Epic Seven's 8th anniversary, we prepared with the mindset that we must adapt to survive"
items.summary: ©INVENToday (29th), Super Creative held "Succession of Eternity," an event celebrating the 8th anniversary of its hero collector turn-based RPG Epic Seven, at Hyundai Department Store Sinchon U-PLEX.
items.content:
Offline mode, simultaneous enhancement of PvE and PvP, and a side story to flesh out the lore

Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ©INVEN Today (29th), Super Creative held "Succession of Eternity," an event celebrating the 8th anniversary of its hero collector turn-based RPG Epic Seven, at Hyundai Department Store Sinchon U-PLEX. The 8th anniversary celebration featured a variety of programs for players, including a meetup between developer personnel and pre-invited players, as well as a month-long collaboration cafe.

Ahead of Succession of Eternity, the 8th-anniversary update released on August 27 introduced an offline Battle Delegation mode that allows farming even when the game is closed, story content for the First Era—the original Epic Seven world prior to Ras—and "Call of Chaos," a new mode that streamlines real-time PvP into a more casual experience while adding roguelike elements. Additionally, several upcoming changes were teased, including a Chaos Zero Nightmare collaboration in September, the addition of a permanent roguelike PvE mode called "Dimensional Exploration," and a Steam launch in the second half of this year.

As Epic Seven moves forward by gradually stepping away from elements it had previously adhered to, what is its ultimate direction? Prior to the meetup with players, we spoke with Producer Kwang-jin Tak and Development Director Dae-gyun Huh at the venue.

Q. Epic Seven has reached its 8th anniversary. How do you feel? Also, it has been a very long time since you held a user and media event—is there a special reason for this?

PD Kwang-jin Tak: Thank you for coming today. Under the excuse of developing and servicing the game, we haven't had many opportunities to speak with you directly. Realizing that this was an area where we fell short, we organized this gathering with the media and players for the first time in a long while. Moving forward, we will make sure to meet more often with good news.

Honestly, the 8th anniversary doesn't quite feel real yet. When we first started, I never imagined what the 8th anniversary would look like, and I believe getting to this point is entirely thanks to the support of our players. Because of that, we were able to try many new things. Reaching the 8th anniversary was never our end goal; we see it as a step in moving further forward. Today's event is an extension of that journey.

DD Dae-gyun Huh: Epic Seven has continued to host anniversary events, and we are deeply grateful for the immense interest shown every time. There is plenty of positive feedback as well as constructive criticism, but we view all of it as care and affection for the game, and we intend to listen closely and make improvements. We hope everyone enjoys the event, and today especially, we hope it becomes an occasion where everyone can smile and have fun.

Q. With Epic Seven turning 8, what do you think is the biggest change over the past 8 years from the development team's perspective? Also, what core value do you aim to preserve throughout its service?

PD Kwang-jin Tak: The biggest change is how the development team perceives Epic Seven. Early in service, there were many shortcomings, so we focused on polishing and completing the game. Now that it is on a solid track, we are looking for ways to introduce changes while respecting the play experience that players have built over time.

The value we have sought to protect from the very beginning to now is, naturally, charming characters and high animation quality. We view the fun of turn-based strategy stemming from combinations of Heroes and gear as Epic Seven's identity, and we have constantly contemplated ways to reinforce it.

Q. As you look toward the 10th anniversary, what is your vision for continuing to receive players' love for another 10 years?

PD Kwang-jin Tak: To last for more than 10 or 20 years, we believe even higher quality is needed. This applies to both art quality and content quality. Rather than releasing content frequently, we think it is crucial to craft it properly before presenting it to players. We want to respect the gameplay experience players have had so far while introducing new content distinct from existing modes.

DD Dae-gyun Huh: Epic Seven is often called a "salmon game" because many players step away for a while and return during specific updates. This shows a solid core player base already exists, and we believe the service can only be maintained long-term if this core player base and new players integrate well. Therefore, we pay close attention to narrowing the gap between different player demographics.

items.title: Epic Seven’s 8th Anniversary Update: Everything Revealed
Epic Seven Unveils 8th Anniversary Updates Including Steam Store Page Launch
items.summary: Provided by Epic Seven ©Epic Seven Smilegate announced on Monday, August 24, that Epic Seven, the mobile turn-based strategy RPG developed by Super Creative, revealed details on ne...
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on Provided by Epic Seven

Smilegate announced on Monday, August 24, that Epic Seven, the mobile turn-based strategy RPG developed by Super Creative, revealed details on new content, events, and the opening of its Steam store page through the showcase video "Infinity," celebrating its 8th anniversary of official launch.

The showcase video was released on the official Epic Seven YouTube channel at noon on Saturday, August 22. In the video, Executive Producer Kwang-jin Tak and Development Director Dae-kyun Heo, who lead the planning and development of Epic Seven, shared future update plans and details on interactive offline events for the 8th anniversary.

The news of Epic Seven's expansion to Steam attracted the most attention in the video. Epic Seven will officially launch on Steam within this year, as part of a platform expansion addressing global players' demand for a Steam release. To this end, the Steam store page opened on August 22, launching a Wishlist Event that grants various currencies and items based on the number of wishlists reached. Players can play on Steam through account transfer supported by STOVE, and a new server will also be provided alongside the official Steam launch. The new server will operate as an independent matchmaking server for a set period to accommodate players starting Epic Seven for the first time. In addition, controller support will be added to the Steam service to offer a unique gameplay experience. The exact launch schedule will be announced at a later date.

Various 8th anniversary update details were also unveiled. A new side story Episode, "Paradise Lost," which covers the earliest era in the Epic Seven lore—where the world repeatedly falls into ruin and is rebuilt—will begin on August 27, with new heroes such as "Lisette" and "Uncharted Pioneer Politis" introduced sequentially. A collaboration with Smilegate's another popular IP, Chaos Zero Nightmare (CZN), is also underway. Key combatants from CZN will be added as Epic Seven heroes, along with "Dimensional Exploration," a new roguelike PvE mode. Meanwhile, a new real-time PvP mode, "Call of Chaos," will be added to the World Arena. Players can look forward to unpredictable battles in every match using "Destiny," a powerful effect chosen during combat.

In terms of quality-of-life improvements, the introduction of an offline feature for battle delegation (repeat battling) drew significant interest. Once added, players can collect growth materials through repeat battles while offline, which is expected to further ease the burden of hero progression.

Information on offline events scheduled through the second half of the year, starting with the 8th anniversary celebrations, was also announced. On Saturday, August 29, the "Festival of Everlasting Successors" will be held on the 12th floor of Hyundai Department Store Sinchon Branch with approximately 160 players. Executive Producer Kwang-jin Tak and Development Director Dae-kyun Heo will attend the event to communicate directly with fans. Furthermore, a collaboration cafe will operate on the B2 floor of Hyundai Department Store Sinchon Branch for about a month, from August 29 to September 30. In addition, the global esports tournament to determine the ultimate Epic Seven World Arena champion, the Epic Seven World Championship (E7WC 2026), will kick off on September 12 with in-game qualifiers. The Grand Finals are scheduled to take place on Saturday, November 28 at the Lotte World Tower Super Plex in Jamsil.

Meanwhile, an 8th anniversary event packed with generous rewards will begin on August 27, offering all players a total of 1,260 free Covenant Summons and the bunny girl-themed "Majestic New Moon Luna" skin, which won first place in a player popularity poll.

Detailed information about Epic Seven can be found on the official Epic Seven community and official YouTube channel.

items.title: Epic Seven Releases New Shepherd of the Dark Diene Update
items.summary: Epic Seven has released a brand-new Moonlight Hero, Shepherd of the Dark Diene, along with additional content in the latest update
items.content:
Posted in: Games , Mobile Games , Video Games | Tagged: Epic Seven , Smilegate , Super Creative

Epic Seven has released a brand-new Moonlight Hero, Shepherd of the Dark Diene, along with additional content in the latest update

Smilegate and developer Super Creative has launched a new update for Epic Seven , bringing with it a new character. Players now have access to Shepherd of the Dark Diene, a new Moonlight Hero who brings a different set of attacks and more to the fray, along with a New Year's event to kick off 2026. We have more details here as the content is live today.

Shepherd of the Dark Diene is a country girl who, after encountering a black wolf in the forest, forms a contract with Noias, the Dark Spirit Lord, who has appeared for the first time in centuries. Driven by her admiration for the Hero "Aki" and her unwavering determination, she embarks on her journey to save the world. But as her journey unfolds, it begins to transform into something dark and twisted. She is a 5★ Dark elemental Mage Hero who can lead battles to her advantage by utilizing various effects that trigger when she is granted "immortality." Her Skill 1, "Crimson Claws," inflicts rupture on the enemy, and a successful attack always results in a critical hit. Damage dealt increases proportionally to the caster's max Health. When the caster is granted immortality, it triggers a Dual Attack from the ally with the highest Attack.

Her Skill 2, "Noias's Guidance," grants immortality for 1 turn at the start of battle. Additionally, when someone uses a Soulburn, dispels all debuffs from the caster before activating "Dark Moon," which dispels buffs from all enemies, grants immortality to the caster for 3 turns, and increases Combat Readiness by 35%. Her Skill 3, "Endless Darkness," inflicts seal on all enemies for 2 turns, and attacks them before decreasing Combat Readiness by 30%. Also, a successful attack always results in a critical hit. When the caster is granted immortality, they ignore Effect Resistance.

To celebrate the New Year, Smilegate will also be running several in-game events. First, the "New Year Check-In Event" will run for three weeks until the 22nd. Players can log in to receive a New Year's greeting from Merurin. The New Year's Gift Chest includes Lv. 88 Equipment and "Fire Horse Stamps," which can be used in concurrent events. The second event, "Collect New Year Stamps," will run during the same period. By consuming Energy daily, players can obtain "Leif" and the event currency, "Fire Horse Stamps." In the third event, "New Year's Gift Arrived!," players can use the "Fire Horse Stamps" earned from the two events mentioned earlier to open random chests containing rewards such as MolaGora and Charms. Finally, in the "Merurin's Lucky Pouch" event, players can clear simple missions to earn various rewards, including a final reward of 1,000 Skystone.

items.title: Epic Seven Esports Viewership and Statistics
Epic Seven Review
items.summary: Epic Seven comes about as close to breaking the mold as I've ever seen. Although it does this at the cost of incorporating some gameplay mechanics better
items.content:
Though Epic Seven is worth a download, you're going to have to try it for yourself to see if it's worth the space on your phone.

What are some of the first things that come to mind when you think of mobile gacha games? Shallow gameplay, incessant power creep, and punishing summoning systems pretty much top the list for anyone even vaguely familiar with the genre. Some of the gaming industry’s worst practices are synonymous with gachas, and even the most respected gacha titles in the market can’t shake all the genre’s shortcomings.

Fire Emblem Heroes is still one of the biggest poster children for unbridled power creep despite Intelligent Systems’ improvements to the game following its release. Fate Grand Order distinguishes itself from its peers through excellent aesthetics and well-crafted narratives. But even after receiving six years of updates, its gameplay mechanics remain archaic, and its summoning system lacks many quality of life changes adopted by its contemporaries. Two steps backward almost always follow each step forward, and it’s almost impossible to find a title that doesn’t choose to die on one of these hills of gacha vices.

Epic Seven comes about as close to breaking the mold as I’ve ever seen. Although it does this at the cost of incorporating some gameplay mechanics better suited to an MMORPG than a mobile game, it proves an interesting if not worthwhile experience. Your mileage may vary, but the game’s appealing visuals, welcome summoning system, and sprawling amount of content make it worth taking a hard look at.

Epic Seven is a turn-based RPG in which you build teams of up to four heroes. Each hero is associated with one of five elements: earth, ice, fire, light, and dark. The latter two elements are vulnerable to each other, while the first three are strong or weak against one another in a rock-paper-scissors arrangement. Heroes also come in various classes. For example, thieves embody the archetype of high damage output but low survivability, and soul weavers fill the healer role while offering supporting abilities such as team resurrection. I recommend a balanced team of a tank, two damage dealers, and a healer for general PvE content. Still, the classes offer enough flexibility to support plenty of experimentation.

Every hero boasts two basic skills and an ultimate skill. While you may assume this skill system is shallow at first glance, the limited skill selection makes gameplay more cohesive and tight-knit. Every skill feels impactful, from basic skills to high-end ultimate abilities. Buffs and debuffs attached to most skills enhance this feeling. They often result in extreme damage and healing numbers that leave you supremely satisfied, and they can make lower-rarity heroes just as fun to use as five-star ones. For example, defense break, a common debuff, reduces a target’s defense by a massive 70%!

Sadly, Epic Seven ‘s story is not its selling point. You play as Ras Elclare, a human avatar of a faction of benevolent gods. Thanks to certain malevolent gods, Ras’ world is trapped in a cycle of constant destruction and rebirth. He journeys to end this vicious cycle once and for all. Unfortunately, the game’s meager writing and unwillingness to see certain plot twists through mar the story. After its introductory chapters, the game wraps consequential plot points in a noticeable layer of armor it refuses to shed, making the journey feel more like a long tutorial than an engaging piece of fiction. The campaign improves as you progress, but by and large, Epic Seven ‘s narrative goes in one ear and out the other.

Fortunately, you can sink your teeth into a lot more than the campaign. On the PvE end of things, you can dive into standard material/equipment grinding maps. Or you can explore sprawling labyrinths with a clever morale system that keeps you from steamrolling the entire map in one go. If you’re looking to test your team to its limit, you can try to clear Automaton Tower and Abyss, which handsomely reward you if your team is up to the task. Side stories — temporarily available sidequests — provide additional story content, though they amount to little more than snippets of lore and some extra loot.

Arena mode provides most of the game’s PvP content. In arena, you battle against other players’ teams to climb the ranks. You can also battle other players in real-time in the world arena. After joining a guild, those who prefer teamwork can participate in guild wars, a slightly modified version of arena with rarer rewards.

The absence of significant power creep among new heroes helps keep gameplay balanced. In fact, many of the most powerful characters to this day have been available since close to release. Generally speaking, the design philosophy behind new heroes focuses on breadth and emphasizes new combat styles or fresh takes on already-existing ones.

Epic Seven has you covered even if you enjoy the hero-collecting aspect of gacha games over their actual gameplay. You earn skystones, the game’s premium currency, through quests, campaign progression, and in-game events. You mainly use skystones to acquire covenant bookmarks, a currency you can spend to summon new heroes. Though you can trade skystones for bookmarks directly, players seeking to maximize efficiency may want to use skystones to refresh the secret shop on the home screen. By doing so, you can usually acquire bookmarks at a more favorable rate. The game also incentivizes you to refresh the secret shop by giving each refresh a chance to yield mystic medals. You can use mystic medals to obtain rarer light and dark heroes, though doing so significantly dents your reserves of gold.

The game’s normal banners — events that offer boosted odds of summoning certain heroes — are similarly generous. Though they only offer a 1% chance to summon a specified five-star hero (that banner’s “rate-up” hero), you’re guaranteed to summon the hero after 120 summons. What’s more, when you net a five-star hero, the banner ensures the hero you summon is its rate-up hero. As a result, you no longer need to worry about summoning pity breakers, unwanted five-star heroes that reset enhanced summoning odds. With just a bit of research on banner rotations and three to four weeks of diligent saving, you can grab any five-star hero that isn’t light or dark.

It’s a shame that the game locks five-star light and dark heroes behind more demanding summoning systems. You’ll have to save currency for months to obtain these heroes. Fortunately, they’re only relevant in PvP, and completing the campaign rewards you with one of six powerful, meta-relevant light and dark five-star heroes. So you’re not entirely out of luck if you’re interested in five-star heroes of the light or dark variety.

Epic Seven hits the brakes on the fun train once you get to its hero leveling and upgrade systems. Leveling demands extensive grinding, and you can take very few shortcuts to dodge this bullet. You also need to promote heroes to six stars to reach their maximum potential, which requires sacrificing five other five-star heroes. The game offers heroes designed for sacrifice, so you don’t need to burn through all your precious summons to obtain six-star ones. However, these sacrificial heroes mostly come in two, three, or four-star rarities, meaning you have to grind to promote them to five stars first.
